units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
They become more embarrassed than ever.
You must think this very strange.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: A little singular. Pardon me for saving so.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: half apologetic, half huffy.
The young lady was married secretly; and her husband has forbidden her, it seems, to declare his name. It is only right to tell you, since you are interested in Miss--er--in Violet.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: sympathetically.
I hope this is not a disappointment to you.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: softened, coming out of his shell again.
Well it is a blow. I can hardly understand how a man can leave a wife in such a position. Surely it's not customary. It's not manly. It's not considerate.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: We feel that, as you may imagine, pretty deeply.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: testily.
It is some young fool who has not enough experience to know what mystifications of this kind lead to.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: with strong symptoms of moral repugnance.
I hope so. A man need be very young and pretty foolish too to be excused for such conduct. You take a very lenient view, Mr Ramsden. Too lenient to my mind. Surely marriage should ennoble a man.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: sardonically.
Ha!
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Am I to gather from that cacchination that you don't agree with me, Mr Tanner?
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: drily.

Get married and try. You may find it delightful for a while: you certainly won't find it ennobling. The greatest common measure of a man and a woman is not necessarily greater than the man's single measure.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Well, we think in America that a woman's moral number is higher than a man's, and that the purer nature of a woman lifts a man right out of himself, and makes him better than he was.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: with conviction.
So it does.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: No wonder American women prefer to live in Europe! It's more comfortable than standing all their lives on an altar to be worshipped. Anyhow, Violet's husband has not been ennobled. So what's to be done?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: shaking his head.
I can't dismiss that man's conduct as lightly as you do, Mr Tanner. However, I'll say no more. Whoever he is, he's Miss Robinson's husband; and I should be glad for her sake to think better of him.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: touched; for he divines a secret sorrow.
I'm very sorry, Malone. Very sorry.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: gratefully.
You're a good fellow, Robinson, Thank you.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: Talk about something else. Violet's coming from the house.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I should esteem it a very great favor, men, if you would take the opportunity to let me have a few words with the lady alone. I shall have to cry off this trip; and it's rather a delicate--
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: glad to escape.
Say no more. Come Tanner, Come, Tavy.
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: He strolls away into the park with Octavius and Tanner, past the motor car.
Violet comes down the avenue to Hector.
Are they looking?
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: No.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: She kisses him.
Have you been telling lies for my sake?
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: Lying! Lying hardly describes it. I overdo it. I get carried away in an ecstasy of mendacity. Violet: I wish you'd let me own up.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: instantly becoming serious and resolute.
No, no. Hector: you promised me not to.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: I'll keep my promise until you release me from it. But I feel mean, lying to those men, and denying my wife. Just dastardly.
units.name: HECTOR

units.text: I wish your father were not so unreasonable.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: He's not unreasonable. He's right from his point of view. He has a prejudice against the English middle class.
units.name: HECTOR
